alternatives: Current BM25 passage search with the same segmentation and passage budget.
Keep BM25 as the production baseline and test BM25 plus dense rank fusion. Treat reranking as a separate ablation, not part of the default candidate.
brief.applicability: On identical long-paper questions and cached passages, compare BM25, BM25+dense fusion, then fusion+reranker. Blindly assess whether answer-support spans enter the top-k and whether the fixed reader gives supported answers; measure local indexing, retrieval, and end-to-end latency.
constraints: No paid model APIs, GPU, or training in this pilot.
Development results are provisional; do not represent independent human support review.
brief.expected_signal: Promote hybrid only if it recovers at least 3 more support spans among 40 questions and loses no more than 1 span found by BM25, with no decrease in independently reviewed supported answers. Reranker must improve at least 2 additional support-span hits beyond hybrid; latency ceiling unset pending hardware measurement.
brief.hypothesis: Keep BM25 as the production baseline and test BM25 plus dense rank fusion. Treat reranking as a separate ablation, not part of the default candidate.
limitations: This draft is a decision aid; it has not been executed or independently validated.

observations.text: Qwen3-8B code-execution paper reader has 35 replay-verified trajectories. On 40 development questions, v5 SFT changed recorded execution-error episodes from 22 to 1; provisional supported-answer passes on 20 answerable cases stayed at 3 for base and v5.

unknowns: SciRet uses CORD-19 with pseudo-relevance labels, so its retrieval scores are not a QASPER prediction. A generic cross-encoder may reduce precision in this domain; paper-specific retrieval and reranking costs are unknown.
